- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for risk reversal or market panic.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent high), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 5% of spike magnitude.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (price drops 5%+ from recent peak), model often fails to recognize it; add 1–2% downward bias in next forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict early in the period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is bullish; apply 1–2% downward adjustment to first 5 forecasts.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “1.00” extremes, model exhibits overconfidence bias; apply 2–3% downward adjustment to all forecasts in that cycle.
